title: Status Effects
wikitext:
[[Category:Mechanics]] '''Status Effects''' are various types of effects that are applied to your character, enemies, or allies. Status Effects have a duration, which determines the length of time the effects will last. And a Potency, which determines the strength of its effects. Duration is indicated by the number at the top of the status icon marked in seconds, and potency is indicated by the number at the bottom of the status icon. Status effects are divided into three types, Buffs, Debuffs, and Neutral status effects. These can be differentiated via the color of the status potency indicator, being green, red, and white respectively. Status Effects do not stack their potency or duration, and a player/mob can only apply one instance of a status effect to a target at a time. Status Effects use the highest potency, and duration of the applied status to determine their potency and duration.
  • e.g. if a player were to apply {{StatusEffects|Regen}} at 0.2 potency for 20 seconds, and then apply {{StatusEffects|Regen}} at 1 potency for 2 seconds, Regen will be at 1 potency for 20 seconds.
However if a status effect is applied by multiple sources onto the same player/mob, the duration of each application is respected when determining at what potency an effect applies.
  • e.g. if player A. were to apply {{StatusEffects|Regen}} at 0.2 potency for 20 seconds, and player B. were to apply {{StatusEffects|Regen}} at 1 potency for 5 seconds, then Regen will function at 1 potency for 5 seconds, and at 0.2 potency for the remaining 15.
  • Damage over Time statuses like {{StatusEffects|Bleed}}, {{StatusEffects|Burn}}, and {{StatusEffects|Poison}} instead stack per source, i.e. player A. and player B. can both apply {{StatusEffects|Bleed}} and each instance of the status will do damage separately
When the source of a status effect dies, the status effect will expire, regardless of remaining duration.

title: Enemy Modifiers
wikitext:
[[Category:Mechanics]]
==Overview==
Every mob (With the exception of Bosses) has a slight chance to spawn with a modifier, indicated by a variety of colored particles emitting from them.

Each variant boasts increased damage, health, tenacity, and special loot drops.

Keep in mind that guaranteed enchant/armor drops can be nullified by [[Trophy Hunter]]

Modifiers are half as likely to happen in [[Frontier Village]] and twice as likely to happen in the [[Deadlands]] and [[Icy Plateau]]

==List of Modifiers==
===Magical===
A mystical blue glow. Magical mobs have a blue colored name.

Special Properties:
*Guaranteed chance to drop an [[Enchantments|enchanted]] armor piece

[[File:Magical Enemy.png|300px]]

===Corrupted===
A dark purple glow. Corrupted mobs have a purple colored name, and have a much higher chance of spawning during the [[Encroaching Void]] event.

Special Properties:
*High chance to drop [[Binded Corruption]]
*High chance to drop [[Enchantments|Corrupt Enchantment]]

[[File:Corrupt Enemy.png|300px]]

===Bloody/Bloodied===
A blood red glow. Bloody mobs have a red colored name, and can only spawn during [[Blood Moon]] events.

Special Properties:
*Guaranteed chance to drop something
*High chance for the item to have [[Enchantments|Thirsty Enchantment]]
*Low chance to drop [[Brilliant Dust]]
*Increased player detection range, gains the ability to automatically target players if it couldn’t before

[[File:Bloody Enemy.png|300px]]

===Legendary===
A bright yellow glow. Legendary mobs have a yellow coloured name.

Special Properties:
*Guaranteed chance to drop [[Enchantments|Legendary Enchantments]]
*Guaranteed chance to drop [[Brilliant Dust]]
*Gives +1 SP on kill

[[File:Legendary Enemy.png|300px]]

==Giant Enemies==
Enemies can very rarely spawn as Giant, increasing their size, damage, tenacity, and health. The chance is greatly increased during the [[Blood Moon]]. Giant enemies drop more items than usual upon being defeated, and can also drop [[Brilliant Dust]].

There are three tiers of Giant enemies: Big, Colossal and Titanic, with stats and drops increasing accordingly.

[[File:Giant Enemies.png|800px]]

Colossal and Titanic enemies trigger a message in the chat when they spawn or are killed. They also feature boss health bars that show when you are close enough.

Giant enemies can have normal modifiers alongside their Giant trait, if the enemy features a boss health bar, the color of the respective modifier will show there as well.

Additionally giant enemies have an increased chance to drop enchants depending on their tier:
* 1.5x for Big enemies
* 2x for Colossal enemies
* 3x for Titanic enemies

title: Infusion
wikitext:
[[Category:Mechanics]] Infusing a piece of [[Equipment]] grants the user the piece's perk and half of its base stats, upgraded and enchanted pieces can be infused, but will not retain their upgrades or enchantments. Once an item is inserted it CANNOT be withdrawn. Infusing a second item replaces what was in the infuser before and does not give it back. Infusing an item at the helmet, chestplate or leggings infuser will cost a [[Binding Orb]], while the ring infuser is free, provided that the rift in the [https://voxlpedia.miraheze.org/wiki/Map?marker=Void_Rift@598.040:499.650#tabber-Ice_Caverns Ice Caverns] dungeon was completed prior to accessing it. The infusers can be found in the following locations : * Head Slot: [https://voxlpedia.miraheze.org/wiki/Map?marker=Infusers@2309.180:3196.160#tabber-Lowlands Vinelands] * Chest Slot: [https://voxlpedia.miraheze.org/wiki/Map?marker=Infusers@3010.830:1291.430#tabber-Lowlands Icy Plateau] * Legs Slot: [https://voxlpedia.miraheze.org/wiki/Map?marker=Infusers@4856.570:9357.800#tabber-Lowlands Deadlands] * Ring Slot: [https://voxlpedia.miraheze.org/wiki/Map?marker=Ring_Infuser@549.350:567.810#tabber-Ice_Caverns Ice Caverns] ==Gallery== [[File:Vinelands Infuser.png|425px|thumb|left|link=|[https://voxlpedia.miraheze.org/wiki/Map?marker=Infusers@2309.180:3196.160#tabber-Lowlands Vinelands Helmet Infuser Location]]] [[File:Icy Plateau Infuser.png|425px|thumb|left|link=|[https://voxlpedia.miraheze.org/wiki/Map?marker=Infusers@3010.830:1291.430#tabber-Lowlands Icy Plateau Chestplate Infuser Location]]] [[File:Deadlands Infuser.png|425px|thumb|center|link=|[https://voxlpedia.miraheze.org/wiki/Map?marker=Infusers@4856.570:9357.800#tabber-Lowlands Deadlands Leggings Infuser Location]]]

title: Crafting
wikitext:
[[Category:Mechanics]] The crafting menu can be accessed through a crafting bench, located within most towns. At the crafting bench, you can craft certain items, gaining crafting XP every time you craft. XP gained depends on the item crafted, and when the users crafting levels up they gain [[Mechanics#Currency|1 SP]] and access to more crafting recipes. When crafting [[Equipment]], there's a chance for it to have an [[Enchantments|Enchantment]], this chance increases the higher the users crafting level is. Upgraded and enchanted equipment cannot be used for crafting.

title: Armor Penetration
wikitext:
[[Category:Mechanics]] ==Defense==
dmgTaken =
if def% > 0, dmg / (1 + def%)
if def% < 0, dmg * (1 + |def%|)

* Positive Defense decreases incoming damage, negative defense increases incoming damage * Every unique source of defense is multiplicative to eachother, rather than additive ** Defense stats however, are additive with eachother, i.e. physical and air defense are additive when reducing air damage taken ==Armor Penetration== Where pen is a decimal, 10 armor penetration is = 0.1 pen, If defense ≤ (pen + 0.2), armor multiplier = defense - pen *If defense - pen > 0, then armor multiplier acts as positive defense **i.e. the multiplier is 1 / (1 + armor multiplier) *If defense - pen < 0, then the armor multiplier acts as negative defense **i.e. the multiplier is 1 - armor multiplier If defense > (pen + 0.2), armor multiplier = defense / (1 + 5 * pen) *Armor multiplier acts as positive defense **i.e. the multiplier is 1 / (1 + armor multiplier) ===Examples=== For example, against an enemy with 100% physical defense with a 10 damage physical attack At 80 armor penetration *1 - 0.8 = 0.2 *10 / (1 + 0.2) = ~8.33 physical damage taken At 120 armor penetration *1 - 1.2 = -0.2 *10 * (1 - (-0.2)) = 12 physical damage taken At 20 armor penetration *1 / (1 + 5 * 0.2) = 0.5 *10 / (1 + 0.5) = ~6.67 physical damage taken ==Notes==
  • True Damage does not benefit from Armor Penetration, Armor Debuffs, or other Armor Reduction sources
  • Multiple sources of Armor Penetration are additive with eachother regardless of the type they negate
  • Armor loss from Armor Debuffs is also additive with Armor Penetration
  • Armor Penetration and Armor Debuffs do not apply to non-stat based defense effects, i.e. {{StatusEffects|Reinforce}}

title: Cooldowns
wikitext: [[Category:Mechanics]] ==Cooldowns== A cooldown is a timer that prevents the use of a skill or effect until the timer has fully elapsed, Cooldown Reduction is an effect that reduces this timer. Weapon Art and Rune Cooldowns are limited to integers, and decrease every 'game tick', which will typically occur once every second. This means that cooldowns that aren't whole numbers are floored to the next whole number. * e.g. a 10.99 second cooldown becomes a 10 second cooldown. Weapon Art and Rune cooldowns can only be reduced up to a 1 second minimum. Cooldown Reduction effects can typically be divided into three categories, Cooldown Reduction, Cooldown 'Speed', and Flat Cooldown Reduction. ===Cooldown reduction list=== '''For a list of all perks and effects that provide Cooldown Reduction, ''' '''see [[Perks#cooldown_reduction|Cooldown reduction list]].''' ===Cooldown Reduction=== 'Cooldown Reduction' effects reduce the cooldown of a Weapon Art/Rune by a set percentage. Application of this type of CDR can be done like so : * FinalCD = BaseCD * (1 - CooldownReduction%) Notable perks/effects of this type include the following : * [[Races#tabber-Elf|Elf]] * [[Races#tabber-High_Elf|High Elf]] * [[Channeled Weapon]] * [[Divinity]] * [[Magic Surge]] * [[Mageling Spirit]] ===Cooldown Speed=== Cooldown 'Speed' effects apply similarly to normal Cooldown Reduction effects, but follow a diminishing curve for its effectiveness. Termed as 'cooldown speed' because it can be represented as increasing the effective time elapsed per game tick. Application of this type of CDR can be calculated with the following formula : * FinalCD = BaseCD / (1 + CooldownSpeed%) * e.g. at +50% Cooldown Speed, a 10 second cooldown would become a 6.66 second cooldown. Though due to game ticks, the cooldown is actually reduced to 6 seconds. Notable perks/effects of this type include the following : * [[Caster]] * [[Emotional]] * [[Mage Rage]] * [[Poison Acceleration]] * [[Runic Winds]] * [[Star Friendship]] * [[Wave Rider]] * [[Whirlwind]] ===Flat Cooldown Reduction=== Flat Cooldown Reduction effects reduce the cooldown of a Weapon Art/Rune by a flat second amount. Due to cooldowns being unable to be reduced in decimal amounts, these effects instead will only activate after it accumulating to an integer, i.e. 1 second. *e.g. [[Shamanic Flow]] at 1 perk amount will only take effect every 2 hits. Notable perks/effects of this type include the following : * [[Shamanic Flow]] * [[Power Surge]] ===Other Cooldown Effects=== While there are three main categories of cooldown reduction effects, there are also cooldown increases, and effects that set the base cooldown to a different value. Cooldown Increases increase the cooldown of an effect by a set amount or percent, notable examples of this include the following : * [[Voltaic Body]] There are also effects that change the base cooldown to a different value. Examples of these perks/effects include the following : * [[Draconic Blood]] * [[Heat Drill]] * [[Gladiatorial Rage]] A distinction from other cooldown reduction/increase effects is important here, as some perks use the base cooldown of an effect for their own effects. ==Examples== It should also be noted that different sources of Cooldown Reduction, and Cooldown Speed are multiplicative with each other. * e.g. When you have more than one source of Cooldown Reduction, or Cooldown Speed they are applied like so : * FinalCD = BaseCD * (1 - cooldownReductionA%) * (1 - cooldownReductionB%) / (1 + cooldownSpeedC%) / (1 + cooldownSpeedD%) For a practical example, a build with [[Races#tabber-High_Elf|High Elf]], 3 [[Channeled Weapon]], 1 [[Caster]], and 1 [[Whirlwind]] using [[Weapon_Arts#storm_stomp|Storm Stomp]], which has a 20 second base cooldown. * BaseCD * (Channeled Weapon) * (High Elf) / (Caster) / (Whirlwind) * 20 * (1 - (20% + 5%*3)) * (1 - 25%) / (1 + 10%) / (1 + 30%) = 6.81818181818, which is rounded to a 6 second cooldown. {{Cooldowns}}

title: Summons
wikitext: [[Category:Mechanics]] Summons are allied mobs summoned by the player. ==Summon Stats== Summons have separate stats from the player, and scale their strength with the player's level and summon boost stat. A summons max HP and Damage are equal to the following, provided no other influence from perks or other effects : *Base * (1 + summonBoost * (1 + level/80)) **Where Base is equal to the Base HP of the mob, or the Base Damage of the attack in question Summon max HP remains static from summoning, any effect that influences summon max HP will only apply when a minion is summoned. * i.e. when summoning at 100% summon boost, the summoned mobs max HP will remain the same even when swapping equipment to a set with 150% summon boost, or 50% summon boost. Summon damage scales with the players current summon boost, but only up to the amount of summon boost the player had when the minion was summoned. * i.e. when summoning at 100% summon boost, the summoned mobs damage will remain unchanged when swapping equipment to a set with 150% summon boost, but will be reduced when swapping equipment to a set with 50% summon boost Summons also have other stats, like tenacity and defense boosts. These are typically inherent to the mob itself, but can also be influenced by certain perks. ==Summon Decay== Summons also possess decay, losing a percentage of their HP per second. The decay rate of a minion is determined by the minions source, i.e. what perk/item summoned the minion, and the users summon boost. Summon Decay% = baseDecay/(1+summonBoost%) The following is a list of the base decay value for each "summon source" {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center;" ! Source !! Decay% |- | [[Possession]] || 1.5% |- | [[Spore Trooper]] || 1% |- | [[Croakernaut Rune]] || 2% |- | [[Pack Leader Rune]] || 4% |- | [[Sporeling Toss Rune]] || 2% |- | [[Swarm Rune]] || 2% |- | [[Weapon_Arts#blessedlings_summon|Blessedlings Summon]] || 2% |- | [[Weapon_Arts#mage_bomber_summon|Mage Bomber Summon]] || 3% |- | [[Weapon_Arts#skeletal_woof_summon|Skeletal Woof Summon]] || 1% |- | [[Weapon_Arts#toaladin_summon|Toaladin Summon]] || 1% |- | [[Weapon_Arts#undead_buni_summon|Undead Buni Summon]] || 2% |- | [[Weapon_Arts#infernal_legion|Infernal Legion]] || 5% |} Summon decay remains static from summoning, any effect that influences summon decay will only apply when a minion is summoned. Additionally, [[Sacrificial Summoning]] reduces summon decay, while [[Trusty Servant]] removes it from affected summons. ==Summon Perk Interaction== Summons are separate from the player, and do not receive benefits from their perks unless stated otherwise. * e.g. [[Smoldering]] will not provide a 20% damage bonus to summons, but they obviously receive the benefits of [[Sweet Tooth]], and can be buffed by [[Inspiration]] or [[Blessing]] Certain summon perks only apply to summons when they are spawned, while other perks apply to summons adaptively. Summons can only receive healing and buffs from the summoner. A player can have a maximum of 15 summons summoned at once, this limit can be increased with [[Swarm]], or limited to a single summon with [[Trusty Servant]] For a list of summon related perks, see [[Perks#summoner|Summoner]]

title: Damage Type and Scalings
wikitext:
[[Category:Mechanics]]
'''Damage Scaling(s)''' are what determines the boosts an attack scales off of. Damage Type is the output of your damage. '''Damage Type''' and Damage Scaling are completely independent of eachother. ==='''Damage Scaling'''=== * '''Damage Scalings''' multiply the corresponding boost stat to obtain effective boost * In the cases of multiple scalings, they are all additive with eachother * For example on an attack with, at 1.1 '''Air''' Scaling with +50% '''Air''' Boost, and 0.5 '''Magic''' Scaling with +25% '''Magic''' Boost, the total effective boost would be 1.1 * 50% + 0.5 * 25% = 67.5% * To apply this value to our attack, we add a constant 1 to obtain our multiplier, using the numbers from our previous example would look like this :
** dmg * (1 + (1.1 * 50%) + (0.5 * 25%))
** dmg * (1 + 67.5%) ==='''Damage Type'''=== * '''Damage Type''' determines how damage is distributed. It uses the total damage and multiplies it by your damage type. * For example, let's say your total damage is 100. If you had the damage types of 0.7 '''Fire''', and 0.3 '''Magic''', the attack would deal 70 '''fire''' damage and 30 '''magic''' damage. If you had +1 [[Dark Magic]] adding 0.2 '''Hex''' Type to this attack, it would deal an additional 20 '''hex''' damage. * Damage Types don't always add up to 1.0 * Damage Types have NOTHING to do with scaling

title: Currency
wikitext: [[Category:Mechanics]] '''Currency''' in voxlblade can be divided in to two main types, Voxos (V$) and SP. Voxos are a resource gained by doing quests, killing mobs, completing dungeons and selling items at shops, the player is only able to have up to 100,000 V$ at once. Shop buildings have a V$ icon above their door, and the "DESTROY" button in the users inventory changes to "SELL" while in a shop. Voxos can be used to buy armor, upgrade gear, transfer enchants, and as a trading fee. Every trade has a fee of at least 25V$, and an additional 1/3rd of the traded items sell value. SP is a resource gained by leveling up (+5 SP), completing [[Dungeons#Daily_Challenges|Daily Challenges]] (+5 SP), completing certain quests (+1 SP), leveling up crafting (+1 SP), and defeating legendary mobs (+1 SP). SP is used to [[Weapons|upgrade your sword]], transfer [[Brokkr|certain types of weapons between slots]], or learn guild [[Cantrips]]. All SP spent is refunded upon using the [[Lost_Shrine#tabber-Shrine_of_Regret|Shrine of Regret]], and all SP spent on handles is refunded upon joining the [[Monk|Monk Guild]]

title: Temperature
wikitext:
[[Category:Mechanics]] When in a hot or cold location, the player will gain negative effects based on their temperature, indicated by a meter above the health bar visible in these locations. The temperature of the player, and the severity of the negative effects increases based on time spent in these locations.
While in hot locations gain {{StatusEffects|Sweating}} which increases damage taken by up to 70% based on the players current temperature, while in cold locations gain {{StatusEffects|Cold}} which reduces damage dealt by up to 25% based on the players current temperature.
When the temperature indicator points fully towards the right or left, the player will gain either {{StatusEffects|Overheating}} or {{StatusEffects|Freezing}} respectively. {{StatusEffects|Overheating}} causes the player to take 2% of their maximum HP per second as half true damage and half fire damage, while {{StatusEffects|Freezing}} instead causes players to take 2% of their maximum HP per second as half true damage and half air damage. These effects will no longer deal damage if the player is below 10% of their maximum HP.
All of the effects of temperature can be nullified by {{StatusEffects|Heating}} for cold biomes and {{StatusEffects|Cooling}} for hot biomes respectively.
The following locations are a list of the "hot and cold" locations present in-game * [[Caci Field]] * [[Deadlands]] * [[Icy Plateau]] * [[Ice Caverns]] (Cold Modifier)

title: Stats
wikitext:
[[Category:Mechanics]] Stats Boosts are the main way in which the player is granted bonuses to their character, present on all types of [[Equipment]], [[Weapons]], and [[Guilds]], with a stat overview accessible by the green + in the bottom left of the inventory menu. title: Poise
wikitext:
[[Category:Mechanics]] [[Category:Incomplete]]
<onlyinclude>'''Poise''' is a [[Mobs|Mob]] stat that governs how much Poise Damage an enemy can take before staggering.

Poise is typically found on bulkier, more stun resistant mobs, but can also be found on any mob with a [[Enemy_Modifiers|Modifier]].

When a mob is Poise-broken, it is stunned for '''~'''5 seconds and all of its positive defenses are nullified for the duration of the stun, for 15 seconds after a Poise-break no more poise damage can be dealt to that target. Poise also decays overtime at x% (?) of a mobs max Poise per second.</onlyinclude>

title: Critical Hit
wikitext:
[[Category:Mechanics]] [[Category:Incomplete]] A '''Critical Hit''' is a type of hit that multiplies its damage by its critical damage multiplier. A critical hit is indicated by a brighter text-outline on the damage indicator. ===Critical Chance=== Critical Chance is influenced by the users Dexterity Boost and a variety of perks. Perks and effects that increase critical chance or influence whether an effect is a critical or not can be divided into two categories, effects that influence your "Natural Critical Chance", and effects that don't influence natural critical chance. A "Natural Critical Hit" is one sourced from your natural critical chance, the distinction is made because certain effects scale with your natural critical chance or only activate on natural critical hits. Effects/Perks that contribute to Natural Critical Chance contain the following :
  • Dexterity Boost (increases critical chance at a rate of 10:1)
  • [[Flowing Crits]]
  • [[Seismic Momentum]]
  • [[Spell Slinger (Perk)|Spell Slinger]]
  • [[Sharp Crits]]
  • {{StatusEffects|Perfection}} ([[Perfection]])
  • [[Heightened Reflexes]]
Natural Critical chance can not be negatively affected by proc coefficient, but can be positively affected. * i.e. an attack with 0 proc coefficient has the same chance to crit as an attack with 1 proc coefficient, and an attack with 2 proc coefficient has double the critical chance of an attack with 1 proc coefficient Effects/Perks that influence whether you crit or not, but are not natural critical hits/do not increase natural critical chance are the following :
  • {{StatusEffects|Critical Boost}}
  • [[Venom Eater]]
  • [[Thief Training]]
  • [[Carrying Winds]]
  • {{StatusEffects|King's Luck}} ([[Caci King Spirit]])
Notably these effects that increase critical chance are not additive with natural critical chance, but instead a separate critical roll. * i.e. with 20% natural critical chance, and 20% critical chance from [[Carrying Winds]], the chance for a hit to crit is equal to 1 - (1 - 20%) * (1 - 20%) = 36% instead of 40% ===Critical Damage=== Critical hits cause hits to deal more damage compared to a non-critical hit, the magnitude of which is determined by the critical damage multiplier. The base critical damage multiplier is 150% (1.5x), and can be increased or decreased by a variety of perks and effects. Critical Damage is increased directly by the players natural critical chance *i.e. Critical Damage Multiplier is equal to 1 + 50% + naturalCriticalChance To see a list of perks that increase critical damage see [[Perks#crit_damage|Perks]]

title: Damage Calculation
wikitext:
[[Category:Mechanics]] [[Category:Incomplete]] {{Delay}}
DMG =
Base Damage
× Effective Boost Multiplier
× Level Bonus Multiplier
× Damage Bonus Multiplier
× Damage Reduced Multiplier
× Damage Type Multiplier
× Type Specific Multiplier
× Crit Multiplier
× Armor Multiplier
  • Base Damage is the base damage of the source
  • Effective Boost Multiplier is the damage bonus from [[Damage Type and Scalings|Scaling]]
  • Level Bonus Multiplier is the damage bonus from [[Mechanics#Levels|Level]]
  • Damage Bonus Multiplier is the product of multiplying all damage bonuses from perks & other effects together.
  • Damage Reduced Multiplier is the multiplier for how much damage is reduced by damage reducing effects, e.g. {{StatusEffects|Weakness}}, [[Cursed Flames]], [[Pursuit]], etc.
  • Damage Type Multiplier is the damage type of the attack, and perk/effect damage type bonuses that apply to the attack, see [[Damage Type and Scalings]] for more information
  • Type Specific Multipliers are perks/effects that only apply to certain or specific damage types, e.g. {{StatusEffects|Rage}}, {{StatusEffects|Sticky}}, [[Photosynthesis]], etc.
  • Crit Multiplier refers to the critical damage multiplier, and any increases to it from perks or other effects, see [[Critical Hit]] for more information
  • Armor Multiplier refers to enemy armor such as [[Stats|Water Defense]], and armor reducing effects such as {{StatusEffects|Shatter}}, see [[Armor Penetration]] for more information
Typically the order in which bonuses are applied does not matter towards final damage dealt, however certain perks and effects are only affected by certain stages, or only consider up to specific stages when calculating their own damage. Some notable perks/effects of this type contain the following :
  • {{StatusEffects|Lightning Cloak}}
  • {{StatusEffects|Cloudpush}}
  • {{StatusEffects|Cinderpull}}
  • {{StatusEffects|Luminescent}}
  • [[Blub Blub]]
  • [[Fractured Energy]]
  • [[Fungal Prototype]]
  • [[Phantom Pain]]
  • [[Explosive Charge]]
  • [[Ichor Spark]] (Chain Lightning)
  • [[Storm Rend]] (Chain Lightning)
  • [[Curse Rip]]
  • [[Honey Gather]]

title: Forge
wikitext:
[[Category:Mechanics]] '''Forges''' are anvils used to upgrade [[Equipment]] for [[Currency|Voxos]]. Equipment can be upgraded up to a maximum of 5 times, with each upgrade costing more Voxos than the last. Each upgrade costs 500V$, 1,500V$, 2,000V$, 3,000V$, 4,000V$, respectively up to a total of 11,000V$ required to upgrade an equipment piece to its maximum. Upgrading an equipment increases positive stats and negative stats using the following formula :
  • if Stat is positive, stat * (1 + upgradeLevel/10)
  • if Stat is negative, stat / (1 + upgradeLevel/10)
Forges can be found at the following locations, and also be summoned via the [[Knight]] guild [[Cantrips#tabber-Summon_Anvil|Summon Anvil Cantrip]]
  • [[Frontier Village]]
  • [[Bogtown]]
  • [[Cloudlands]]
  • [[Knights Outpost]]
  • [[Ice Caverns#Map|Ice Caverns]]

title: Attack Speed
wikitext: [[Category:Mechanics]] [[Category:Incomplete]] Attack Speed is the property that determines the speed that attack animations can be performed. Attack Speed can generally be divided into three types : * Weapon Attack Speed * Stat Attack Speed * Perk Attack Speed Bonuses within the same type are additive with each other, but multiplicative with the other types ===Weapon Attack Speed=== Weapon Attack Speed is the attack speed value listed on weapon parts, and is the average of both weapon parts. * i.e. [[Basic Handle]] has an Attack Speed of 1, and [[Agile Blade]] has an attack speed of 1.2, so the attack speed value of this weapon combination is equal to (1 + 1.2)/2 = 1.1 * [[Races#tabber-Kitsune|Kitsune]] adds +0.1 to this value ===Stat Attack Speed=== Stat Attack Speed is the attack speed stat found on [[Equipment]] and the [[Enchantments|Quick Enchantment]] ===Perk Attack Speed=== Perk Attack Speed is the attack speed bonuses from [[Perks]], or [[Status Effects|Buffs]] granted by perks. * For a list of related perks see [[Perks#attack_speed|Attack Speed Perks]] * [[Stone Weapon]] is a notable exception, where despite being an attack speed modifier from a perk source it isn't a part of this category, and is instead multiplicative with all attack speed types ==Application== When applying attack speed to an attack, you divide the attacks base attack time by your attack speed multiplier : * AttackTime = BaseAttackTime ÷ AttackSpeedMultiplier * AttackSpeedMultiplier = (weaponAttackSpeed × statAttackSpeedMultiplier × perkAttackSpeedMultiplier) Attack speed bonuses are applied differently depending on whether they're positive or negative. * A positive bonus of x increases attack speed by multiplying it by 1 + x * A negative bonus of x decreases attack speed by dividing it by 1 + |x| For example, a +25% bonus would result in a 1.25x multiplier, while a -25% penalty results in a 0.8x multiplier For example, if you had an attack that had a base attack time of 1, a weapon attack speed of 1.1, a stat attack speed of -25%, and two different attack speed perks that gave +10% and +20% attack speed respectively : * weaponAttackSpeed = 1.1 * statAttackSpeedMultiplier = 1 ÷ (1 + |-25%|) = 0.8 * perkAttackSpeedMultiplier = 1 + 10% + 20% = 1.3 * AttackSpeedMultiplier = 1.1 × 0.8 × 1.3 = 1.144 * AttackTime = 1 ÷ 1.144 = ~0.874 ===Attack Specific Interactions=== Not all attacks are affected by every type of attack speed bonus, or affected by attack speed in the same way. Some attacks have other restrictions or are exceptions to normal attack speed rules. For example [[Weapon Arts]] are unaffected by general Perk Attack Speed bonuses but certain Perk Attack Speed bonuses like [[Quickcast]] and [[Power Inhale]] specifically affect them. __NOTOC__
